reason: Connect the lung side to the pleural membranes as a first step toward linking lung movement to the chest.
expectation: I expect the membranes to attach around the lungs, though I am unsure how the chest connection will be shown.

alternatives.reason: The membranes could instead be attached to the rib cage first, but I chose to start with the lungs.
The control pathway also needs building, but I want to establish the mechanical connection first.

effect: The pleural membranes now cover the lungs, leaving the rib cage connection as the next mechanical step.
reaction: The narrow fluid-filled space makes me curious how chest movement transfers to the lungs.
reason: Connect the covered lungs to the rib cage to build the breathing mechanism.
expectation: I expect the outer pleural membrane to connect the lungs to the chest wall, though the movement may need further parts.

alternatives.reason: The control pathway is also needed, but I want to finish the mechanical connection first.

effect: The lungs are now linked to the rib cage through the pleural interface; the apparatus still needs a breathing muscle and control.
reaction: The interface is visible, but how it transfers chest movement to the lungs remains unclear.
reason: Add the diaphragm to the named breathing-muscle slot before connecting control.
expectation: I expect the diaphragm to fit beneath the rib cage and help change chest volume, although control will still be needed.

alternatives.reason: The control centres and nerves also need connecting, but I want to complete the mechanical apparatus first.

effect: The diaphragm is fitted beneath the rib cage; the control pathway still needs to be built.
reaction: The placement is clear, but the result does not yet show how the diaphragm moves air.
reason: Connect the control centres to the motor nerves; it is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect a nerve pathway from the control centres toward the breathing muscles, though it may still need fitting to the apparatus.

effect: The control centres and nerves form a breathing drive, with CO₂ feedback indicated; it still needs connecting to the apparatus.
reaction: The feedback is interesting, though the inset does not explain how CO₂ changes the rhythm.
reason: Fit the breathing drive into the remaining control slot; it is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the drive to connect to the breathing muscles and complete their control, possibly showing how breathing moves air.

effect: The completed apparatus explains how the diaphragm expands the chest and pulls the lungs outward through the pleural interface, while elastic recoil helps air leave.
reaction: The paired breathing views resolve my earlier uncertainty about how the parts move air.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the breathing drive was most worthwhile: the resulting illustration plan links the diaphragm, pleural interface and lung recoil to airflow.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the diaphragm was clear but somewhat thin on its own; its immediate result showed placement without explaining movement.

surprise.text: The breathing-drive picture introduced blood CO₂ feedback, although it did not explain how CO₂ changes the breathing rhythm.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless: the named slots and compatible options made the assembly sequence clear, even where the mechanism was explained only later.

continue.text: I would be somewhat interested in another chapter if it continued connecting structures to their functions, though this chapter's mostly straightforward fittings offered limited meaningful choice.
